A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Token Hidden Reward work. All pages, including appendices, are readable through text extraction and visual inspection. Existing tables, figures, equations, and sections can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original GRPO/THR training experiments on Qwen and Llama models, including greedy accuracy, Pass@K results, ablations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds parameter sweeps, convergence diagnostics, a clip-high comparison, and token-frequency analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The THR definition, dominant-token mask, sign-based advantage reweighting in Equations (4)–(5), and GSPO integration remain unchanged. Appendix E tests existing parameters and explains the retained threshold without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MATH levels 3–5 and evaluate the same six math benchmarks. Appendix E uses retained math coverage; its MATH validation curves and reflection-token analysis introduce no distinct task or input scenario.

E2.justification: Appendix E.3 adds an evaluated clip-high comparator against GRPO and THR on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B in Table 13. Existing comparisons with Pass@K-mixed, COV-KL, GSPO, and positive/negative-only training remain.

E3.justification: Section 6 changes the reported gradient updates per training step from four to 32; Appendix E.2 specifies 1,280 updates over 40 steps. This substantially revises the stated training budget without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. New experiments also introduce broader p sweeps, clip-high at 0.28, longer convergence traces, and a reflection-token frequency metric.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's retained ablations and entropy/token analyses, Appendix E adds positive and negative p sensitivity studies, validation and reward trajectories examining convergence, reflection-word frequency analysis, and measurements of the fraction of tokens retained. These substantially expand checks of parameter dependence and the proposed mechanism.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables and training curves introduce no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their values, while Appendix E adds substantial results. Table 11 newly reports 37.6% average greedy accuracy at p=0.05; Table 13 reports average Pass@256 of 74.4% for clip-high and 76.7% for THR. Tables 15–16 add reflection frequencies of 0.34%/0.36%/0.55% and retained-token fractions of 18%/14%. These are additional findings, not same-setting gains between versions.

T1.justification: The THR definitions, Theorem 3.1, Corollary 4.2, GSPO formulas, and Appendix D derivations connecting Pass@K reweighting and entropy are retained. The added appendix contains empirical analyses without new formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about influential tokens, sign-guided exploration/exploitation, and generalization across objectives and model families. Appendix E supplies additional support without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds interpretations favoring milder positive p for the 1.5B model, warning of excessive exploitation, and linking reflection-word frequency to corrective behavior. It also qualifies dynamically filtered rewards as imperfect correctness measures and attributes lower token retention in the 7B model to greater confidence.

D1.justification: v4 clarifies prompt-batch accounting and total gradient updates, specifies the new parameter sweeps and clip-high setting, and supplies the reflection-word list in Table 14. Existing hardware, rollout lengths, checkpoint-selection rules, and runtime measurements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and main related-work discussion remain unchanged. Appendix E.3 additionally positions THR against Yu et al.'s clip-high exploration approach; v3 cited that work for dynamic sampling but did not make this comparison.

P1.justification: The main narrative and existing section order are largely retained. v4 adds the focused More Studies appendix, acknowledgments, and an LLM-use disclosure, alongside limited wording clarifications such as specifying observed correct responses.

P2.justification: v4 adds a substantial appendix display set: parameter-sweep tables, convergence and reward plots, a clip-high comparison, and reflection/retention tables. The ICLR layout also resizes and redistributes existing displays. Figures 1–10 retain their content; their relocation does not constitute new evidence.

improvement.justification: Appendix E improves support for parameter selection, training convergence, and comparison with clip-high, while the corrected update accounting improves reproducibility. These strengthen an otherwise retained paper. The reflection analysis remains an indirect lexical proxy for successful correction, and run-to-run uncertainty remains unreported, limiting the overall gain.
